units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
In less than half an hour. He has a capital appetite, thank God.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: And a taste for tobacco, too.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I found my father's pipe in my room--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Aha--then that accounts for it!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: For what?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: When Oswald appeared there, in the doorway, with the pipe in his mouth, I could have sworn I saw his father, large as life.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: No, really?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oh, how can you say so? Oswald takes after me.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, but there is an expression about the corners of the mouth--something about the lips--that reminds one exactly of Alving: at any rate, now that he is smoking.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Not in the least. Oswald has rather a clerical curve about his mouth, I think.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, yes; some of my colleagues have much the same expression.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: But put your pipe away, my dear boy; I won't have smoking in here.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Does so.
By all means. I only wanted to try it; for I once smoked it when I was a child.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: You?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes. I was quite small at the time. I recollect I came up to father's room one evening when he was in great spirits.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oh, you can't recollect anything of those times.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, I recollect it distinctly. He took me on his knee, and gave me the pipe. "Smoke, boy," he said; "smoke away, boy!" And I smoked as hard as I could, until I felt I was growing quite pale, and the perspiration stood in great drops on my forehead. Then he burst out laughing heartily--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: That was most extraordinary.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: My dear friend, it's only something Oswald has dreamt.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No, mother, I assure you I didn't dream it. For--don't you remember this?--you came and carried me out into the nursery. Then I was sick, and I saw that you were crying.--Did father often play such practical jokes?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: In his youth he overflowed with the joy of life--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: And yet he managed to do so much in the world; so much that was good and useful; although he died so early.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, you have inherited the name of an energetic and admirable man, my dear Oswald Alving. No doubt it will be an incentive to you--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: It ought to, indeed.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: It was good of you to come home for the ceremony in his honour.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I could do no less for my father.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: And I am to keep him so long! That is the best of all.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: You are going to pass the winter at home, I hear.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: My stay is indefinite, sir. But, ah! it is good to be at home!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Beaming.
Yes, isn't it, dear?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Looking sympathetically at him.
You went out into the world early, my dear Oswald.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I did. I sometimes wonder whether it wasn't too early.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oh, not at all. A healthy lad is all the better for it; especially when he's an only child. He oughtn't to hang on at home with his mother and father, and get spoilt.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: That is a very disputable point, Mrs. Alving. A child's proper place is, and must be, the home of his fathers.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: There I quite agree with you, Pastor Manders.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Only look at your own son--there is no reason why we should not say it in his presence--what has the consequence been for him? He is six or seven and twenty, and has never had the opportunity of learning what a well-ordered home really is.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I beg your pardon, Pastor; there you're quite mistaken.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Indeed? I thought you had lived almost exclusively in artistic circles.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: So I have.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: And chiefly among the younger artists?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, certainly.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: But I thought few of those young fellows could afford to set up house and support a family.
units.name: MANDERS
